messages.subject: [statnet_help] summary shows wrong results, when treating an undirected graph to directed
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] summary shows wrong results, when treating an undirected graph to directed
messages.body_plain:
Hamid,

I'm guessing you were looking for each undirected edge to be replaced by 
a mutual pair of edges?  Simply using set.network.attribute to change 
the directed network attribute from F to T won't do that; since 
undirected networks are stored in what amounts to upper triangle form, 
the edges will all be replaced by a single directed edge in the upper 
triangle.  There may be another function in network to do what you want 
directly, but I don't know of it. (Anyone?)  In the meanwhile, you can 
achieve the same thing with an extra slice of R code.  Following on your 
set.network.attribute line, add:

flomarriage[,] <- flomarriage[,] + t(flomarriage[,])

This simply transposes the underlying sociomatrix and then takes the 
maximum value of the original and transposed matrices; in other words, 
it brings the 1s in the upper triangle down to the lower as well.  Voila:

 > summary(flomarriage ~ edges + triangle)
    edges triangle
       40       24

Steve





On 5/9/2012 2:09 PM, Hamid Ghofrani wrote:
> Dear All,
> Hopefully I am not asking a trivial question . I need to treat an 
> undirected net as directed. for example, the flomarriage is undirected so
>> summary(flomarriage ~ edges + triangle)
>    edges triangle
>       20        3
>
> Now, if I define it as directed
>
> set.network.attribute(flomarriage,"directed",T)
>> summary(flomarriage ~ edges + triangle)
>    edges triangle
>       20        3
>
> the summary command still shows the results for the undirected network.
> Am I doing something wrong? Is there any other way to force an 
> undirected network to be directed?
> Thank you,
> Hamid

ones.  Thus, as.network(1*(M>0)) should do the trick.

From: Lewis, Kevin <kmlewis@fas.harvard.edu>
Date: Tue, Dec 6, 2011 at 10:02 AM
Subject: RE: [statnet_help] one ergm for multiple networks
To: Christian Steglich <c.e.g.steglich@rug.nl>, statnet help mailing
list <statnet_help@u.washington.edu>


hi christian,

i had a related earlier question on this too, and so can pass along
the advice i received from steve and pavel. i'll caution, however,
that while this indeed provided me with a solution for my problem that
makes intuitive sense to me (and seems to directly parallel the
"structural zeroes" situation in Siena), there may be other reasons
for which this fix is undesirable/inappropriate, especially for the
case of multiple networks? so i will still be curious to hear if
others have further thoughts.

basically you can do exactly what you suggest- create a joint
adjacency matrix of all networks- and then i'm aware of two possible
ways to prohibit ties "between" networks:

1) more straightforward: create a node attribute that has a different
value for membership in each of the different networks; include a
"nodemix" term in your model, and use the "base" argument to only
include those effects from the mixing matrix that correspond to ties
ACROSS networks; and fix those parameters at -Inf (i have had mixed
experience with this in the past... sometimes you may not have to fix
the parameter because ergm will recognize that no ties are present and
do this for you automatically... sometimes it does not and so you have
to do this manually using offset, see below).

2) more cumbersome: basically the same thing, but do this using an
edge covariate instead of a node covariate. in other words, create a
matrix where values for ALL ties WITHIN networks are set to zero, and
ALL ties ACROSS networks are set to one, feed this into your model
using an edgecov term, and again fix that effect at -Inf using the
offset() function, e.g. offset(edgecov(X)).

i hope this is helpful... but others please let us know if for some
reason this approach is problematic! or if there is an easier approach
i'm unaware of. best wishes,

-kevin

From: statnet_help-bounces@mailman2.u.washington.edu

To: statnet help mailing list
Subject: [statnet_help] one ergm for multiple networks

Hello,

is it possible to use the ergm-package for a simultaneous analysis of
multiple networks (in my case: of same size and same content)? I know
that this can be done in PNet and Stocnet-SIENA with the help of
'structural zeros', i.e., by creating a joint adjacency matrix of all
networks' nodes and differentiating between "unconnected" and
"unreachable by design". But PNet and Stocnet-SIENA both require
interactive clicking through Windows menus, and I'd prefer to do this in
R, so a solution in the ergm-package would be preferable. Is there one?

Greetings,
Christian


PS - I realise that related questions have been asked before - without
getting an answer - by Vic Louisier, or Moses Boudourides.

iterations? Is that a setting we could override?

Thanks, and happy holidays!
Balazs

messages.subject: [statnet_help] set edge attributes memory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Jennifer.  A matrix can't be of class network; do you mean that you 
are using an adjacency matrix?  That aside, if you are assigning that 
matrix as an attribute to each edge, you are making as many copies of it 
as you have edges in the graph.  That could easily explain the growth in 
your data size.  (Do you mean instead to assign a numerical attribute to 
each edge?  That's rather different from assigning a network or 
adjacency matrix to each edge....)

Hope that helps,

-Carter

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Albert.  Yes, R's protection stack can be frustratingly small, and 
this can cause problems with delete.vertices in large graphs.  It's on 
the list to fix for the next network package release.  In the interim, 
another approach is to create a new graph and write the edge information 
into it instead of deleting vertices.

Hope that helps,

-Carter

[1] 12635
> length(unique(FromTo))
[1] 12635


If we construct this identifier in Michal's example we see, as expected, that the number of unique From/To combinations is less than the total number of edges and equal to the sum of the adjacency matrix. So the constructed identifier is a way to indicate when there are multiple edges:

> eln<-network.edgelist(n)

> nFromTo<-1000*eln[,1]+eln[,2]
> length(nFromTo)
[1] 3
> length(unique(nFromTo))

Jeremy,

As Martina wrote, you indeed counted each tie twice based on the
edgelist because you used 'length', which for a matrix returns number
of elements, not the number of rows. You should have used 'nrow(el)'.
That does not solve the problem though.

If the number of ties in the edgelist is correct, that is 12635, and
the network is undirected then the adjacency matrix should be
symmetric implying 16486/2=8243 ties. My guess is that you have some
duplicated ties in your edge list (the network being a multigraph)
which are ignored when producing? the adjacency matrix.

In 'igraph' the default action for multigraphs when creating the
adjacency matrix is to count the multiple ties and increase the
corresponding values in the adjacency matrix. Hence the sums agree in
your example. In the "network" package, creating adjacency with as
matrix by default returns a binary matrix, even if there are multiple
ties present, as in the following example:

> n <- network.initialize(3)
> n
Network attributes:
? vertices = 3
? directed = TRUE
? hyper = FALSE
? loops = FALSE
? multiple = FALSE
? bipartite = FALSE
? total edges= 0
? ? missing edges= 0
? ? non-missing edges= 0

Vertex attribute names:
? ? vertex.names

> add.edge(n, 1,2)
> add.edge(n, 2,3)
> add.edge(n, 1,2)
> m <- as.matrix(n, "adjacency")
> sum(m) # here you are expecting 3
[1] 2
> as.matrix(n, "adjacency")
? 1 2 3
1 0 1 0
2 0 0 1
3 0 0 0



~michal

> Ayn and Michal,

> can include the package name into the function call. That makes certain that
> I'm using the correct method, and masking is not the issue.
>
> Unfortunately that doesn't change the answer.
>
>> is.directed(nw)
> [1] FALSE
>> el <- as.matrix.network.edgelist(nw)

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM with Endogenous Terms
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

The answer is no.  If your model does not include dyadic dependent terms, 
then it is not necessary to use MCMC for the estimation, so there is no 
MCMC related SE.

If you believe there is dyadic dependence in the network, then you will 
need to represent this in the model -- by using a term (or terms) that 
captures the dependence.  What do you mean by "inherent dependence"?

best,
Martina

>
> If I estimate an ERGM model that does NOT include endogenous network terms 
> (e.g., isolates, mutual, triangle) and ONLY includes exogenous covariates

> coefficient/standard error BUT do NOT include a MCMC standard errors.

> My question: Are the reported standard errors corrected for the dyadic

> statistical model is used to correct them?  (An article citation here would

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Triad census & edges
messages.body_plain:
Hi Amiyaal,

You cannot add edges as both a constraint or a model term; it must be 
one or the other.  If it's a constraint then it's not allowed to vary, 
and if it's not allowed to vary, then you can't do inference on it. 
Whether you chose to add it as a term or a constraint depends on the 
hypothesis that you're trying to test, and the theoretical seting that 
you're working with.  Is there a reason to believe that the random 
process you're exploring would generate the same number of ties with 
each alternative realization? Or is the actual number of edges 
stochastic as well?

Yours,
Steve

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Generating graphs with a fixed minimum distance
messages.body_plain:
Dear Hamid,

As I understand your problem, you want to find, *by any method*, an
undirected graph in which there exists at least one pair of nodes
that are of minimum distance apart of at least 10.  If this is a
correct interpretation of your problem then you don't need a
computer program to find one.  Here are some examples that satisfy
your conditions:

(1) The linear graph with 11 nodes x(1), x(2), ... x(11), where x(i)
is only connected to x(i+1), for 1 <= i <= 10.  Here x(1) and x(11)
are of distance 10 apart.

(2) Example (1) immediately generalizes to any tree graph which
contains a linear subgraph of at least 11 nodes.  Such trees are
easily constructed, and in abundance.  Here the path in the graph
which connects any pair of nodes of minimal distance apart >= 10 is
unique.

(3) Consider the single cycle graph (a linear graph on N nodes where
the first and last nodes are connected).  If N is odd where N = 2n+1
and n >= 10 then every node in the graph participates  in 2
node-pairs having minimal distance apart >= 10.  If N is even where
N = 2n and n >= 10 then every node participates in a unique
node-pair having minimal distance apart >= 10.

(4) Example (3) generalizes to other multiply connected graphs, such
as a single cycle graph in which the various cycle members have
hangers-on.

I hope this is of some help.

Eugene Johnsen, Professor Emeritus
Department of Mathematics
University of California, Santa Barbara

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Stepping algo and constraints
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet developers,

I think that the stepping algo, as it is coded in the ergm package
2.4-3, doesn't take into account the "contraints" argument defined in
ergm() functions (actually I need a maxout=5 constraint).

I created here some simple code to show you the problem:

#####
library(ergm)

# We simulate a network under the maxout constraint:
net <- simulate(network(50) ~ edges, theta0 = -1, constraints = ~
bd(maxout = 5))
plot(net)
max( rowSums( net[,] ) )

# model formula
f <- net ~  edges

#model estimation
m1 <- ergm(formula = f, theta0 = "MPLE", constraints = ~ bd(maxout = 5),
control = control.ergm( check.degeneracy = FALSE, style = "Stepping",
stepMCMCsize = 300, gridsize = 1000, metric = "lognormal"), burnin = 1e
+4, MCMCsamplesize = 1e+3, interval = 1e+4, maxit = 1, verbose = F )

m1$coef # BINGO, underestimation of the edge param.

# goodness of fit:
m1gof <- simulate(object = f, theta0 = m1$coef , nsim=100, burnin=1e+4,
interval=1e+4, basis = NULL, statsonly=TRUE, sequential=TRUE,
constraints = ~ bd(maxout=5), control = control.simulate.formula(),
verbose=TRUE)
plot(c(m1gof), type="l",ylim=c(150,250))
abline(a= summary(net~edges) ,b=0, col ="red")
legend("bottomright",legend=c("nb of edges in simulated networks","nb of
edges in observed network") ,fill=c("black","red") )
####

After some tests and verifications, I successfully modified the sources
as follow:

- In the "./R/ergm.R" file, change line 286:
    "Stepping" = ergm.stepping(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
by this one:
    "Stepping" = ergm.stepping(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
constraints,


- In the ".R/ergm.stepping.R" file, change line 39:
	ergm.stepping = function(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
by this one:
	ergm.stepping = function(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
constraints,

- In the ".R/ergm.stepping.R" file, change lines 69 and 161:
        interval=MCMCparams$interval, statsonly=TRUE,
by this one:
        interval=MCMCparams$interval, statsonly=TRUE,
constraints=constraints,

After recompiling the package with these small modifications, I obtain
much better results with the above example.

As, I didn't modify the simulate.ergm file, I'm pretty confident these
modifications won't affect other parts of the package.

Best regards,
Victorin Luisier

P.S: A big thank for the newly added comments in the sources, they are
very useful indeed.

--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Criteria for ergm convergence?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Balazs,

I am working on alternative methods to estimate ERGM.

A problem for the default method in ergm package (Hunter and Handcock,
2006) is that
the approximation used for simulated maximum likelihood may still be very
poor.

This implies that iterating may not give a convergent algorithm.

I suggest you to try with the "Stepping" method based on Hummel et al., 2011.

It is already implemented in ergm package (check the R help of
control.ergm).

I think that it is a great improvement also if it can still suffer in
presence near degeneracy and stability problems.

Marry Xmas to everybody.

Nicola

messages.body_plain:
Dear Statneters,

I have some questions about interaction effects between node attributes. I
hope that you can help me with this.  I already read earlier discussions on
interactions, but they do not deal with my problem exactly.

 

Assume the following: The network to be predicted is directed; the nodes
have one metric attribute X, ranging from 0 to 1. The theory that I use
predicts an interaction, so that when both nodes i and j are high in X, i
becomes more likely to direct a tie at j. However, when either i or j are
low in X, this likelihood should decrease.

 

I implemented this interaction effect between Xi and Xj with a matrix that
stores the products of  Xi and Xj for all pairs of nodes (named XiXj ). My
final model looks like this (plus some other terms):

 

model<- ergm(network ~ edges + nodeicov (X) + nodeocov (X) +  dyadcov
(XiXj))

 

My questions are: 

 

1)      Is this model specified correctly?

2)      More specifically: 

a) When I include the interaction term, do I always have to include the
icov/ocov terms (just as I should include the main effects when testing
interaction effects in linear regression models)?

b) Should I include the interaction matrix as an edge-covariate or as a
dyad-covariate?

c) In my results table (see below), the estimated parameters for the
interaction terms are very high. I explain this as follows: I know that Xj
is an important predictor of the tie from i to j (i.e. when X is included
only as nodeicov/nodeocov, the estimated parameters are 5.46/-0.48). Yet,
the distribution of X among the nodes is right-skewed (with a mean of  .14
and maximal value of .8). Thus, after multiplication, the values in the
cells of the interaction matrix are rather small (typically < .10). Based on
this, in my interpretation, the results indicate that there is an
interaction effect between XiXj and the high parameter estimates for this
effect are due to the small values in the interaction matrix. Do you think
my interpretation is correct or do the high values indicate there is

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Algorithm for building an adjacency array from large (~6000x6000) adjacency matrix
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Algorithm for building an adjacency array from large (~6000x6000) adjacency matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
First time posting. I'm hoping someone can help me through a data issue. I have a large adjacency matrix of production networks. The column represents a unit process (say, Steel milling). The rows indicate prior processes and raw material inputs. So column A might have connections to B and C (listed as rows). Step to Column B and it might have connections to A1 and B1 (these are raw resources listed as rows). Since column A connects to B, the network should also connect to A1 and B1. As I proceed through the columns, each column should end up being a network consisting of all the unit production processes and the raw material inputs. I then want to analyze each production network for certain network metrics and shapes.

I read in the matrix as a directed network. I wrote code that used the reachability function of sna to find all nodes there were reachable from each column node. I then built an adjacency array of all the different networks by zeroing out non reachable nodes in the original matrix and adding it to the adjacency array. Everything worked great on test data.

I tested it on the full matrix and it has been running for 36 hours. It appears that my computer with 12GB of ram is struggling and it's using hard disk writes to virtual memory severely slowing things down. Any suggestions on how to better optimize the reachability calculation or an alternate way to pull these network subsets out of the main adjacency network?

I have copied my code below. Thanks in advance for any advice.

X<- read.csv(file="SampNet2.csv",head=TRUE,sep=",",row.names=2)
labels<-X[1]
SampNet= as.matrix(X[2:8])
#Transpose matrix to reverse edge direction
tSampNet<-t(SampNet)

#plot network to verify
gplot(tSampNet,gmode='digraph',diag=T, usearrows=T, displaylabels=T, label.cex=.5)

#create a reachability matrix
Reach<-reachability(tSampNet)

#Function to extract subnetworks using reachability matrix. 
#each row of the reachability matrix represents a network. Function iterates
#through each row setting non-reachable nodes to zero
#Returns an array of size n equal to the number of columns in the original matrix
#each entry in the array is an adjacency matrix of the subnetwork

ExtNet<-function(x,y) 
{
	n<-nrow(x)
	out<-array(,dim=c(n,n,n))
	for (i in 1:n)
	{
		z<-y
		for(j in 1:n)
		{
			z[,j]<-x[i,j]*z[,j]
			z[j,]<-x[i,j]*z[j,]
		}
	z[is.na(z)] <- 0
	out[,,i]<-z	
	}
	return(out)
}

#Function loses labels for each matrix. NetArray is instantiated. Then must re-add labels 
#to array to preserve
NetArray<-ExtNet(Reach,tSampNet)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Bjorn,

I've had a similar problem in the past.  If you save the output of the
plotting command, something like:

 p1 = plot(newnet1, etc....)
>

you'll see that the coordinates of all the points are saved, and that these
are not the same from one call to plot to the next.

So, you can pull out the coordinates from "p1" (by taking say the min or
max of the x or y values).  More often though, I will just use:

messages.subject: [statnet_help] visualizing networks?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Adrian,

I'm not sure what a matrix diagram is, but if I understand you then  
it's relatively easy to write R code from scratch to do something like  
that.  Here's a little snippet I wrote for a talk that plots an  
adjacency matrix as a white square with black entries where the arcs  
lie:

matplotter <- function(x) {
   if (is.network(x)) x <- x[,]
   n <- dim(x)[1]
   plot(0:n, n:0, type="n", xaxt="n", yaxt="n", xlab="",
        ylab="", bty="n", ylim=c(n,0))
   therows <- row(x)[x>0]
   thecols <- col(x)[x>0]
   rect(thecols-1, therows-1, thecols, therows, col=1)
   rect(0,0,n,n)
}

It should be easy to customize this in many ways (adding color,  
labels, etc.).  To see it used, try

library(ergm)
data(flo)
matplotter(flo)

Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM with Endogenous Terms
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Michael -

On 10/09/2011 05:12 PM, Michael T. Heaney wrote:
> Dear Statnet Community,
>
> If I estimate an ERGM model that does NOT include endogenous network
> terms (e.g., isolates, mutual, triangle) and ONLY includes exogenous
> covariates (e.g., nodecov, dyadcov), then the reported ERGM results
> include the ordinary coefficient/standard error BUT do NOT include a
> MCMC standard errors.
>

Yes - there is no need for MCMC in this case.  (This is actually a 
network logit model -- see also netlogit in sna.)

> My question: Are the reported standard errors corrected for the dyadic
> dependence that is inherent in the network data?

Is there in fact "inherent" dyadic dependence in your data?  If so, why 
are you fitting an independence model?  (To put it another way, if you 
believe that there is dependence, then you should model it.  The 
reported standard error estimates reflect your modeling assumptions.)

> If YES, then what
> statistical model is used to correct them? (An article citation here
> would be most welcome.) If NO, then is there any way to ask the ERGM
> routine to run the MCMC simulation WITHOUT including endogenous parameters?

The MCMC here is a red herring -- it's just used to perform the 
numerical calculations required to obtain the estimates.  I think you 
want to determine whether you really believe you have an autocorrelation 
problem, and if so model accordingly.

Another option, if you are just interested in hypothesis testing for the 
covariate effects, would be to use either netlogit (w/QAP) in sna or the 
netperm package.  The QAP test for netlogit is not known to have great 
properties, so caveats apply; the netlm case is better behaved.  The 
netperm model can also be used in a similar manner, but is more exotic. 
  In any event, all three provide avenues for estimating relations among 
matrices (and testing hypotheses about the same) while controlling for 
within-matrix autocorrelation.

Hope that helps,

-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] one ergm for multiple networks
messages.body_plain:
hi christian,

i had a related earlier question on this too, and so can pass along the advice i received from steve and pavel. i'll caution, however, that while this indeed provided me with a solution for my problem that makes intuitive sense to me (and seems to directly parallel the "structural zeroes" situation in Siena), there may be other reasons for which this fix is undesirable/inappropriate, especially for the case of multiple networks? so i will still be curious to hear if others have further thoughts.

basically you can do exactly what you suggest- create a joint adjacency matrix of all networks- and then i'm aware of two possible ways to prohibit ties "between" networks:

1) more straightforward: create a node attribute that has a different value for membership in each of the different networks; include a "nodemix" term in your model, and use the "base" argument to only include those effects from the mixing matrix that correspond to ties ACROSS networks; and fix those parameters at -Inf (i have had mixed experience with this in the past... sometimes you may not have to fix the parameter because ergm will recognize that no ties are present and do this for you automatically... sometimes it does not and so you have to do this manually using offset, see below).

2) more cumbersome: basically the same thing, but do this using an edge covariate instead of a node covariate. in other words, create a matrix where values for ALL ties WITHIN networks are set to zero, and ALL ties ACROSS networks are set to one, feed this into your model using an edgecov term, and again fix that effect at -Inf using the offset() function, e.g. offset(edgecov(X)).

i hope this is helpful... but others please let us know if for some reason this approach is problematic! or if there is an easier approach i'm unaware of. best wishes,

-kevin

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Modeling Advice
messages.body_plain:
Hello Users:

I'm writing to collect some general advice about modeling a particular type of data. I hope the following longish description of the current modeling puzzle is appropriate for this list, as it involves both theoretical questions and empirical specification questions. I have estimated a series of ERGM and Siena models in my attempt to explain the network variation in my data, but I have encountered numerous problems relating to degeneracy and model specification.  Ultimately, my goal is to appropriately model the relationships of actors in two different legislative institutions and test for the presence of bridging-ties.  Below, I describe my data, my hypothesis, and the modeling approaches I've attempted. I hope to gather some insight from the list about the most appropriate method for testing the claims of interest.

The data are from two legislative bodies (US and EP).  In the US case, we have three time periods/waves, and in the EP we have two waves (total of 5 adjacency matrices).  The dependent variable describes the relationships between legislative actors through legislative member organizations (LMOs). We have a number of dyadic and nodal attribute variables as well about the actors.  The hypothesis I seek to test is whether there are bridging-ties among the legislators through their LMO memberships.  We have no hypotheses across the US and EP--only within legislature hypotheses.

One approach I've tried is to simply calculate betweenness (in the SNA package) for each network of legislators in each time period, add this as a vertex attribute, and estimate an ERGM, in which betweenness is a nodal-covariate, in addition to a series of other endogenous structural terms and exogenous covariate controls.  I can do this 5 times--one ergm for each legislative time period. For example:

mymodel1<-ergm(cauc109.aff.dichot.net~edges+triangle+density+twopath+nodecov("between")+nodematch("party")+nodematch("statecode")+nodematch("gender")+nodematch("leader")+nodematch("black")+nodecov("term")+nodecov("electpct"), eval.loglik=TRUE, seed=123, interval=1000, burnin=100000, MCMCsample=1000000, verbose=T)

However, these models have difficulty with convergence and fit.  I am unable to obtain MCMC standard errors, and even after numerous attempts at respecification the diagnostics suggest that fit may be problematic.  Note that every run of a model takes a number of hours on a high memory machine so there is a limit to the number of iterations I can do.

Another approach is to use Siena.  Siena should allow me to take advantage of the longitudinal nature of the data (even though in the EP we only have two waves--which is limiting for Siena).  I have been able to estimate some Siena models using these data; however, suspicions about correlations between structural terms have forced me to reduce the model quite a bit.  The EP models I have run are very pared down and still suggest problems with degeneracy and fit.  The US models have yet to converge after running for several days on the high memory machine.  Experts on the Siena list have warned me about correlations and wondered if Siena was the appropriate architecture for these data.

For example, I have tried the following effects:
> myeffus
   effectName                        include fix   test 
1  constant caucuses rate (period 1) TRUE    FALSE FALSE
2  constant caucuses rate (period 2) TRUE    FALSE FALSE
3  degree (density)                  TRUE    FALSE FALSE
4  betweenness                       TRUE    FALSE FALSE
5  same usstate                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE
6  same usparty                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE
7  same usblack                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE
8  same uswomen                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE
9  usterm similarity                 TRUE    FALSE FALSE
10 uselectpct similarity             TRUE    FALSE FALSE

So my various attempts at testing this hypothesis using these advanced methods have left me frustrated.  While we can (and have) tested the idea using a variety of less sophisticated methods, it seems to me that the advanced statistical methods, such as those available through ERGM and Siena, are designed for exactly this type of modeling; however, I have not been able to achieve satisfactory findings that are reportable. I can continue to try to reparameterize the models to search for fit and to avoid degeneracy, but I would like to hear thoughts of readers of this list regarding:
- the appropriate method for testing the hypothesis
- best practices for iterative modeling and specification for these types of models (given that each iteration is so computationally expensive)
- which architecture (ERGM, Siena, something else?) seems most appropriate for the data

I am happy to collect responses off-list and post a summary to the list later if there is sufficient discussion on some of these items.  I can also provide additional helpful details off list.

Best,

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM with Endogenous Terms
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Michael -

On 10/09/2011 07:28 PM, Michael T. Heaney wrote:
> Dear Martina,
>
> Thanks so much for your quick response.
>
> The problem that I am having is that if I use the endogenous network
> terms, then I am getting errors that say 'Error: cannot allocate vector
> of size 41.5 mb'.
>
> My network has 738 nodes.

What are you putting into the model?  We've fit much larger networks 
(but, of course, a lot depends on the terms you use).

>
> By 'inherent dependence' I mean that since each node appears in the data
> 737 times, I want the standard errors to be computed in a way that
> accounts for the common variance among these 737 observations.
>

The notion of "common variance" is not very helpful here.  How, 
precisely, do you think that the nodes are leading to dependence among 
the dyads?  (There are many ways of thinking about this.)  It sounds 
like you may have in mind sender/receiver effects (i.e., fixed effects 
for rows and/or columns, or "sociality" for both).  This is only one 
form such dependence can take, however -- the Markov graphs represent 
another.

If you were trying to use sender/receiver/sociality terms with a model 
of that size, I imagine you might have run into problems (you are adding 
a vast number of parameters in that case).  If you really think you have 
substantial heterogeneity that can't be captured by degree distribution 
terms (e.g., through gwdegree), then you might want to go the 
permutation test/model route....

-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Modeling Advice
messages.body_plain:
Jennifer

I'm confused about what you are trying to model.  You say you want to
determine if there are bridging ties, but to answer this would not require
an ERGM or SIENA model.  I would ask which ties act as bridging ties and
measure their extent of bridging.  Then I would calculate edge betweenness
to see which ones are in bridging positions  and see if this varies over
time.  If you want to know which nodes act as bridges then you can calculate
betweenness or bridging and see which people are bridges.

-Tom

 

-----Original Message-----

From: statnet_help-bounces@mailman2.u.washington.edu
[mailto:statnet_help-bounces@mailman2.u.washington.edu] On Behalf Of Victor,
Jennifer Nicoll

Sent: Monday, March 12, 2012 9:03 AM

To: statnet_help@u.washington.edu

Cc: Nils Ringe (ringe@wisc.edu)

Subject: [statnet_help] Modeling Advice

 

Hello Users:

 

I'm writing to collect some general advice about modeling a particular type
of data. I hope the following longish description of the current modeling
puzzle is appropriate for this list, as it involves both theoretical
questions and empirical specification questions. I have estimated a series
of ERGM and Siena models in my attempt to explain the network variation in
my data, but I have encountered numerous problems relating to degeneracy and
model specification.  Ultimately, my goal is to appropriately model the
relationships of actors in two different legislative institutions and test
for the presence of bridging-ties.  Below, I describe my data, my
hypothesis, and the modeling approaches I've attempted. I hope to gather
some insight from the list about the most appropriate method for testing the
claims of interest.

 

The data are from two legislative bodies (US and EP).  In the US case, we
have three time periods/waves, and in the EP we have two waves (total of 5
adjacency matrices).  The dependent variable describes the relationships
between legislative actors through legislative member organizations (LMOs).
We have a number of dyadic and nodal attribute variables as well about the
actors.  The hypothesis I seek to test is whether there are bridging-ties
among the legislators through their LMO memberships.  We have no hypotheses
across the US and EP--only within legislature hypotheses.

 

One approach I've tried is to simply calculate betweenness (in the SNA
package) for each network of legislators in each time period, add this as a
vertex attribute, and estimate an ERGM, in which betweenness is a
nodal-covariate, in addition to a series of other endogenous structural
terms and exogenous covariate controls.  I can do this 5 times--one ergm for
each legislative time period. For example:

 

mymodel1<-ergm(cauc109.aff.dichot.net~edges+triangle+density+twopath+nodecov
("between")+nodematch("party")+nodematch("statecode")+nodematch("gender")+no
dematch("leader")+nodematch("black")+nodecov("term")+nodecov("electpct"),
eval.loglik=TRUE, seed=123, interval=1000, burnin=100000,
MCMCsample=1000000, verbose=T)

 

However, these models have difficulty with convergence and fit.  I am unable
to obtain MCMC standard errors, and even after numerous attempts at
respecification the diagnostics suggest that fit may be problematic.  Note
that every run of a model takes a number of hours on a high memory machine
so there is a limit to the number of iterations I can do.

 

Another approach is to use Siena.  Siena should allow me to take advantage
of the longitudinal nature of the data (even though in the EP we only have
two waves--which is limiting for Siena).  I have been able to estimate some
Siena models using these data; however, suspicions about correlations
between structural terms have forced me to reduce the model quite a bit.
The EP models I have run are very pared down and still suggest problems with
degeneracy and fit.  The US models have yet to converge after running for
several days on the high memory machine.  Experts on the Siena list have
warned me about correlations and wondered if Siena was the appropriate
architecture for these data.

 

For example, I have tried the following effects:

> myeffus

   effectName                        include fix   test 

1  constant caucuses rate (period 1) TRUE    FALSE FALSE

2  constant caucuses rate (period 2) TRUE    FALSE FALSE

3  degree (density)                  TRUE    FALSE FALSE

4  betweenness                       TRUE    FALSE FALSE

5  same usstate                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE

6  same usparty                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE

7  same usblack                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE

8  same uswomen                      TRUE    FALSE FALSE

9  usterm similarity                 TRUE    FALSE FALSE

10 uselectpct similarity             TRUE    FALSE FALSE

 

So my various attempts at testing this hypothesis using these advanced
methods have left me frustrated.  While we can (and have) tested the idea
using a variety of less sophisticated methods, it seems to me that the
advanced statistical methods, such as those available through ERGM and
Siena, are designed for exactly this type of modeling; however, I have not
been able to achieve satisfactory findings that are reportable. I can
continue to try to reparameterize the models to search for fit and to avoid
degeneracy, but I would like to hear thoughts of readers of this list
regarding:

- the appropriate method for testing the hypothesis

- best practices for iterative modeling and specification for these types of
models (given that each iteration is so computationally expensive)

- which architecture (ERGM, Siena, something else?) seems most appropriate
for the data

 

I am happy to collect responses off-list and post a summary to the list
later if there is sufficient discussion on some of these items.  I can also
provide additional helpful details off list.

 

Best,

Jennifer Victor

Offhand, it sounds like there is simply not enough memory allocated for your R session.  After all, you are attempting to fit a model with an enormous number of parameters (the sender and receiver effects each have one per node).  Thus, one possibility is to restart R after somehow allowing for more memory.

Another thing you might try is decreasing, not increasing, the value of maxNumDyadTypes.  While this might break something else in fitting such a complicated model--it's hard to predict because a very sparse network might actually still be fine--it might also help with the memory issue because the array of size maxNumDyadTypes * nstats will be smaller.  (In your model, nstats is more than 5000.)

Hope this helps!
Dave

messages.body_plain:
Hi there

I'm trying to fit a linear autocorrelation model using the lnam
function in the sna package.

I've developed a number of possible models with different geodesic
distances, reciprocal and nonreciprocal friends. Lnam will fit a model
when the matrix order is in the correct order, but not if my variables
are ordered to match the order of the relevant person ID's in the
adjacency matrix.

The matrices are typically 647*647 node matrices with 2336 vertices.
My rownames and colnames are a list of ID numbers in the same order,
and I've checked that the one specifications match my original data.
There are no ones on the diagonal.  The matrices produce the following
response from R;

"Error in qr.solve(t(X) %*% X, t(X) %*% W1a %*% y) :  singular matrix
'a' in solve"

I've get the same response testing a variety of subsets of the matrix,
matrices with different levels of geodesic distances, alternative
covariates, alternative dependent variables, matrices transformed into
network objects.

I've been able to get these spatial error models (errorsarlm) and
spatial lag models(lagsarlm) to run in spdep which applies the same
equation and also uses maximum likelihood through "solve" to find a
solution. I was hoping to cross check a couple of the results by
running them in lnam but the inability of lnam to run these models has
made me question the equivalence of the two methods

Does anyone know of a possible solution to the singular matrix
problem? Perhaps something in the settings of lnam or a way to
transform the matrix so that it is no longer singular
(non-invertible)?


Please let me know if any additional details are needed to understand my query


Thank you in advance

Jenny Long
PhD student
University of Auckland

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] error simulating bipartite networks with networksis
messages.body_plain:
Dear Juan,

The problem is that 
simulate(bip1, nsim=1) 

doesn't provide enough information by itself.  To use simulate.network, you'll need to provide information about a model class and the specific parameter values that identify a particular member of that class.  Said member define a probability distribution on the set of all networks, which is something from which one can logically simulate.  So, for instance:

simulate (bip1~edges) # This gives a formula, but still no parameters (however, the ergm package will use 0 as the default parameter).

simulate (bip1~edges, coef=1) # This gives a formula, identifying a model class (ERGMs whose sufficient statistic is the number of edges) as well as a coefficient value.  

Hope this helps.

Best wishes,
Dave

messages.body_plain:
Offhand, it sounds like there is simply not enough memory allocated for your R session.  After all, you are attempting to fit a model with an enormous number of parameters (the sender and receiver effects each have one per node).  Thus, one possibility is to restart R after somehow allowing for more memory.

Another thing you might try is decreasing, not increasing, the value of maxNumDyadTypes.  While this might break something else in fitting such a complicated model--it's hard to predict because a very sparse network might actually still be fine--it might also help with the memory issue because the array of size maxNumDyadTypes * nstats will be smaller.  (In your model, nstats is more than 5000.)

Hope this helps!
Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] normalized centralities for weighted networks
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This illustrates a general point that's worth highlighting for all 
users.  Often the way to accomplish a task in statnet is to write a 
(relatively short) piece of R code that is external to statnet itself. 
This is by design.  The great strength of the R platform is the wide 
range of existing functions (both in base and in the packages) that 
allow many ways to accomplish all sorts of tasks.  We wrote statnet in R 
specifically so that users could draw on all of that.  So when you don't 
see the functionality that you might be expecting in statnet, that 
doesn't mean it's necessarily unavailable, especially if it seems like a 
common task that many would want to do. In those cases, it probably 
reflects the fact that the task requires only a small piece of R code, 
so there was really no need to write a new function.  Unlike stand-alone 
network packages, then, there can be extra legwork to do in terms of 
learning more R.  But the upside is that once you do it, you have great 
flexibility.  Not just for network modeling, but for the entire world of 
statistical computing.

That said, this forum remains the perfect place to ask these questions, 
and hear from other users about how they accomplished a task -- whether 
with a statnet function or R code more generally. Or to share your own 
insights about how to accomplish a network-related task with a 
particularly clever bit of R code that you think others might benefit from.

Cheers,
Steve

> each mode? ergm would then recognize that no within-mode ties existed,
> fix these parameters at negative infinity, and respect this
> restriction during parameter estimation.
> 
>  
> 
> i have another situation where certain actors are not allowed to
> contact each other- but these ?impossible? ties are not structured in
> such a way that i can model them with nodematch terms. in other words,
> they are something like ?structural zeroes? in the language of RSiena-
> and i would like to estimate a model that respects this restriction
> where some ties are not possible. my first thought was to follow the
> same approach as above, but instead of using nodematch terms to
> identify the ?impossible? ties, i would do the same thing with an
> edgecov term. when i run this model, however, ergm does not seem to
> recognize that these ties are impossible in the same way it does for
> the nodematch situation? and so instead of getting a parameter that is
> fixed at negative infinity, i simply get a parameter estimate that is
> strongly negative (say, -16) and becomes even more strongly negative
> with each MCMC iteration.
> 
>  
> 
> my question, then, is whether this approach is problematic for any
> reason? or is this actually a reasonable way to impose ?structural
> zeroes? in the model? it seems the ideal case would be to be able to
> fix this parameter at negative infinity? but if there is not currently
> a way to do this, i want to make sure the approach i?ve taken in
> practice (i.e. letting the edgecov parameter work its way to an
> unstable, but strongly negative value) is not creating other issues of
> which i?m unaware. any help would be greatly appreciated! thanks,
> 
>  
> 
> -kevin

If you are using Windows version of R, consider adjusting the RAM
limit larger than 2G. If you are using the 32 bit version of R, the
max RAM is 3G. It might still not enough for ERGM of a moderate size
network.

ERGM is memory and CPU intensive even for a very small network. You
may need to consider a more powerful machine or pruning your network.

CH

messages.subject: [statnet_help] "network" package masked by "base"
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Martina, that's what the error was implying and I was about to check a list of other mirrors.


Michal is correct; the edgelist has got directed edges going each way between many nodes. I hadn't looked at the data or code in over a year, and I forgot that the edges are recorded as directed.


The test I used is not able to test the multiple edges, as pointed out. Thanks for your help!


The adjacency matrix produced by igraph contains "2's" in the case of reciprocal edges. To verify that it's the same number of undirected edges as I get from "network", I can divide this matrix by two and round up. The matrices are then identical, which confirms that "network" adjacency matrix is doing exactly what I want and counting each linked node pair once.


So the issue of how I came to the unexpected number of edges in the adjacency matrix is resolved.

Sociologically, the edges can be treated as undirected. But the way we collected the data, in iterative waves, the final respondents did not have a chance to confirm the reciprocity, so these return edges aren't in the database, and caused the unexpected asymmetry (due to my short memory). The network modelling will need account for the wave structure of the survey.


-Jeremy

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Interpretation of GWDegree
messages.body_plain:
Dear everyone,

We have run some models with the geometrically weighted degree term
(the model and results attached).

Is it correct to explain the positive effect of GWDegree as an
indicator of anti-preferential attachment (as in Hunter 2007) or
less-hub structures since the Equation 13 in Hunter 2007 suggested
that Alternating-k-star = exp(theta)( 2x Edges - GWDegree)?

The reason we have this question is that some papers  interpreted it
the same as Alternating-k-star such as in
http://www.projectguia.org/documents/research/100813/14_parra_jpah_2009_0295.pdf:
"(with a positive GWDegree) there was a strong tendency for
organizations with high degree (GWDegree) to collaborate with other
organizations that also have high degree."

Your comments will be appreciated a lot.
Best,

Yun Huang

m1<-ergm(co_prop ~ edges + gwdegree(0.69, fixed=T) + gwesp(0.9,fixed=T))

Monte Carlo MLE Results:
                         Estimate Std. Error MCMC s.e. p-value
edges                -13.15707    0.41581     0.098  <1e-04 ***
gwdegree            4.73408    0.33972     0.081  <1e-04 ***
gwesp.fixed.0.9   3.72574    0.05527     0.001  <1e-04 ***


-- 
Yun Huang
Science of Networks in Communities (SONIC)
Industrial Engineering and Management Sciences
Northwestern University
Google Voice: 847-220-7310
Office: FSB 1.459

messages.subject: [statnet_help] "network" package masked by "base"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy,

I can't reproduce your error:

> library(network)
> data(flo)
> nw=network(flo, directed=F)
> dim(as.matrix.network.edgelist(nw))
[1] 20  2
> adjmat<-as.matrix(nw, matrix.type = "adjacency",dimnames=NULL)
> sum(adjmat)/2
[1] 20
>

You mention no namespace... what version of network are you using? 1.5?  If
so, you may want to update 'network'. I'm using 1.7 in the example above

Also, you can explicitly call the as.matrix.network function, rather than
as.matrix:

> adjmat2<-as.matrix.network(nw, matrix.type = "adjacency",dimnames=NULL)
> all(adjmat==adjmat2)
[1] TRUE
>

HTH,

Ayn   :)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy,

'as.matrix' is a generic function which defined in "base" package. The
"network" package provides a method for that generic for network
objects, i.e., as.matrix.network, as Ayn wrote. There is no
'as.matrix' function in the "network" package, only the method. The
user is supposed to call the generic 'as.matrix' and R will
automatically look up the proper method for the object, just like you
did in your example: 'as.matrix(mw, ...)'.

I think the problem must be somewhere else, not with the appropriate
method being selected. R finds the proper method, as you demonstrated
with 'find'. Moreover, you does not seem to have any packages in your
search path that might have resulted in a conflict (AFAIK).

Namespaces should not be a problem, as Ayn wrote, as the "network"
package has a namespace already for some time.

I think you have to be more specific. Perhaps you can provide a small
example data that would reproduce the problem?

~michal

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Latent Cluster Model with package latentnet
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Latent Cluster Model with package latentnet
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Alla,

In case this is still of use, constructing a network with a latent
structure and a particular degree sequence requires more than just
latentnet, since latentnet only deals with unconstrained networks.

One way to do this is to use the fact that conditional on the latent
space positions, a latent space model is essentially an ERGM with a
particularly structured dyadic covariate, so you can use the ergm
package to simulate it.

Let y0 be the network object whose degree sequence you want to "copy",
let Zi be the i'th latent position. Then,

1) Construct a covariate matrix with elements Xij=-|Zi-Zj|.
2) Run something along the lines of 
library(ergm)
y <- simulate(y0~edgecov(Xij),theta0=c(1),constraints=~degrees)

Then y should be a realization of a network with the correct degree
sequence and a latent position structure. You might need to use a long
burn-in.

                          I hope this helps,
                          Pavel

messages.subject: [statnet_help] stepping algorithm trace values
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicola,

I know my reply is late (and that you probably found a solution) but,
anyway, it could be useful for others...

When you download the ERGM package sources on CRAN,

http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/contrib/r-release/ergm_2.4-3.zip

you can slightly modify the ./ergm/R/ergm.stepping.R file by
uncommenting (removing the #) line 206 and 207.

After, you have to recompile the package from these modified sources by
running in a terminal:

R CMD INSTALL ergm/

Or, inside R:

install.packages("<PATH/TO/ERGM/SOURCES>",repos=NULL)

Now, when you use the stepping algo, your ergm object will contain the
informations you need:

mymodel <- ergm(<blablabla_whith_stepping>)
mymodel$allmeanvals # give all mean value parameter estimates
mymodel$allparamvals # give all eta


Best regards,
Victorin

messages.body_plain:
Hi Adrian,

Here is what I do with "ergm". Carter's "sna" package can do a lot more:

library(ergm)
# First get the full geodistance matrices
data(sampson)
a <- ergm.geodesicmatrix(samplike)
a
data(florentine)
a <- ergm.geodesicmatrix(flomarriage)
a
# Not pick some off by edgelists
gd <- function(s,d,nw){ergm.pairgeodesic(as.matrix(nw,mat="edgelist"),
s=s,d=d,directed=is.directed(nw),n=network.size(nw))}
gd(1,3,flomarriage)
gd(1,2,flomarriage)
gd(1,4,flomarriage

Cheers,

Mark

p.s. The "summary" function in "statnet" was designed to get network 
statistics, e.g., summary(flomarriage ~ isolates)

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Isolates in ergm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wincent,

To follow on with that: I agree with Pavel - you would rarely want to 
exclude isolates, and if you did, it should be because you believe that 
they are somehow excluded from the stochastic process you are modeling; 
I have a hard time coming up with a reasonable example, but if you were 
in that case, you would then need to condition your model on no isolates.

Now, assuming you do include the isolates in the network for estimation 
-- whether you then want to explicitly include an isolates term in the 
model or not, or consider some other set of model parameters that would 
address the preponderance of isolates (other degree terms, for instance) 
is really a question of the hypotheses that you are interested in 
testing.  This is a substantive question that only you and your 
collaborators can really answer.

Cheers,
Steve



On 12/24/2011 10:59 AM, Pavel N. Krivitsky wrote:
> Dear Wincent,
>
> The isolates are a part of the information you have about the social
> structure, so they most certainly should be kept in the network. (In
> principle, if you excluded the isolates, you would have to fit a model
> conditional on having no isolates.)
>
>                  I hope this helps,
>                  Pavel

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Stepping algo and constraints
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Victorin.  What you're saying makes sense, and I appreciate the code suggestion!  I'll check this out and try to get it into the next release.

Best wishes,
Dave




On Jan 5, 2012, at 3:16 PM, Victorin Luisier wrote:

> Dear Statnet developers,
> 
> I think that the stepping algo, as it is coded in the ergm package
> 2.4-3, doesn't take into account the "contraints" argument defined in
> ergm() functions (actually I need a maxout=5 constraint).
> 
> I created here some simple code to show you the problem:
> 
> #####
> library(ergm)
> 
> # We simulate a network under the maxout constraint:
> net <- simulate(network(50) ~ edges, theta0 = -1, constraints = ~
> bd(maxout = 5))
> plot(net)
> max( rowSums( net[,] ) )
> 
> # model formula
> f <- net ~  edges
> 
> #model estimation
> m1 <- ergm(formula = f, theta0 = "MPLE", constraints = ~ bd(maxout = 5),
> control = control.ergm( check.degeneracy = FALSE, style = "Stepping",
> stepMCMCsize = 300, gridsize = 1000, metric = "lognormal"), burnin = 1e
> +4, MCMCsamplesize = 1e+3, interval = 1e+4, maxit = 1, verbose = F )
> 
> m1$coef # BINGO, underestimation of the edge param.
> 
> # goodness of fit:
> m1gof <- simulate(object = f, theta0 = m1$coef , nsim=100, burnin=1e+4,
> interval=1e+4, basis = NULL, statsonly=TRUE, sequential=TRUE,
> constraints = ~ bd(maxout=5), control = control.simulate.formula(),
> verbose=TRUE)
> plot(c(m1gof), type="l",ylim=c(150,250))
> abline(a= summary(net~edges) ,b=0, col ="red")
> legend("bottomright",legend=c("nb of edges in simulated networks","nb of
> edges in observed network") ,fill=c("black","red") )
> ####
> 
> After some tests and verifications, I successfully modified the sources
> as follow:
> 
> - In the "./R/ergm.R" file, change line 286:
>    "Stepping" = ergm.stepping(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
> by this one:
>    "Stepping" = ergm.stepping(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
> constraints,
> 
> 
> - In the ".R/ergm.stepping.R" file, change line 39:
> 	ergm.stepping = function(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
> by this one:
> 	ergm.stepping = function(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
> constraints,
> 
> - In the ".R/ergm.stepping.R" file, change lines 69 and 161:
>        interval=MCMCparams$interval, statsonly=TRUE,
> by this one:
>        interval=MCMCparams$interval, statsonly=TRUE,
> constraints=constraints,
> 
> After recompiling the package with these small modifications, I obtain
> much better results with the above example.
> 
> As, I didn't modify the simulate.ergm file, I'm pretty confident these
> modifications won't affect other parts of the package.
> 
> Best regards,
> Victorin Luisier
> 
> P.S: A big thank for the newly added comments in the sources, they are
> very useful indeed.
> 
> --

messages.subject_clean: AW: [statnet_help] Fitting ergm with sender and reciever fails
messages.body_plain:
Dear Arne,

> after playing around with maxNumDyadTypes it seems like my model is
> too complex to converge. Nevertheless, I'm trying to avoid memory
> problems by using a HPC-Cluster (nodes with 64GB Ram) at the moment,
> but do not have any outcome yet.

There is also a problem with your model being

edges + isolates + sender + receiver

Having, edges, sender, and receiver in it means that every vertex's
degree will be modeled exactly. This means that a degree distribution
term like isolates is going to be nonidentifiable, so this model can't
be fit.

> Maybe simplifying the network will help? My network uses multiplex
> edges, choosing only unique edges reduces the number of edges to
> 11.000. Is there a way to include edges weights (from multiple edges)
> into the ergms? The weights are stored in an edge attribute called
> "weight".

ergm doesn't handle multiplex edges at all, so I think that it's already
only looking at unique edges. As for edge weights, that functionality is
in the works, and we hope to release it sometime this year.

                  I hope this helps,
                  Pavel

> Jeremy,

> symmetric implying 16486/2=8243 ties. My guess is that you have some
> duplicated ties in your edge list (the network being a multigraph)
> which are ignored when producing ?the adjacency matrix.

> In 'igraph' the default action for multigraphs when creating the
> adjacency matrix is to count the multiple ties and increase the
> corresponding values in the adjacency matrix. Hence the sums agree in
> your example. In the "network" package, creating adjacency with as
> matrix by default returns a binary matrix, even if there are multiple

>> In this case, sum(adjmat3) equals length(el); respectively, there are the

messages.subject: [statnet_help] problems installing statnet
messages.body_plain:
Dear Elena,
Try using the statnet.org repository.  It's not a CRAN mirror, but (unlike CRAN) it has the most current version of the statnet package.  

To do this, try 
install.packages("statnet", repos="http://www.csde.washington.edu/statnet")

This might not work, as it appears that the problem you're having is with rgl rather than any of the statnet packages.  However, if I remember correctly, there is no strict dependence on rgl in the new statnet so you might be okay.

Best wishes,
Dave

messages.body_plain:
Dear Martina,

Thanks so much for your quick response.

The problem that I am having is that if I use the endogenous network  
terms, then I am getting errors that say 'Error: cannot allocate  
vector of size 41.5 mb'.

My network has 738 nodes.

By 'inherent dependence' I mean that since each node appears in the  
data 737 times, I want the standard errors to be computed in a way  
that accounts for the common variance among these 737 observations.

Any additional advice would be much appreciated.

Thanks.

Michael


Quoting Martina Morris <morrism@u.washington.edu>:

> Hi Michael,
>
> The answer is no.  If your model does not include dyadic dependent  
> terms, then it is not necessary to use MCMC for the estimation, so  
> there is no MCMC related SE.
>
> If you believe there is dyadic dependence in the network, then you  
> will need to represent this in the model -- by using a term (or  
> terms) that captures the dependence.  What do you mean by "inherent  
> dependence"?
>
> best,
> Martina
>
> On Sun, 9 Oct 2011, Michael T. Heaney wrote:
>
>> Dear Statnet Community,
>>
>> If I estimate an ERGM model that does NOT include endogenous  
>> network terms (e.g., isolates, mutual, triangle) and ONLY includes  
>> exogenous covariates (e.g., nodecov, dyadcov), then the reported  
>> ERGM results include the ordinary coefficient/standard error BUT do  
>> NOT include a MCMC standard errors.

messages.body_plain:
Jeremy,

As Martina wrote, you indeed counted each tie twice based on the
edgelist because you used 'length', which for a matrix returns number
of elements, not the number of rows. You should have used 'nrow(el)'.
That does not solve the problem though.

If the number of ties in the edgelist is correct, that is 12635, and
the network is undirected then the adjacency matrix should be
symmetric implying 16486/2=8243 ties. My guess is that you have some
duplicated ties in your edge list (the network being a multigraph)
which are ignored when producing  the adjacency matrix.

In 'igraph' the default action for multigraphs when creating the
adjacency matrix is to count the multiple ties and increase the
corresponding values in the adjacency matrix. Hence the sums agree in
your example. In the "network" package, creating adjacency with as
matrix by default returns a binary matrix, even if there are multiple
ties present, as in the following example:

> n <- network.initialize(3)
> n
 Network attributes:
  vertices = 3
  directed = TRUE
  hyper = FALSE
  loops = FALSE
  multiple = FALSE
  bipartite = FALSE
  total edges= 0
    missing edges= 0
    non-missing edges= 0

 Vertex attribute names:
    vertex.names

> add.edge(n, 1,2)
> add.edge(n, 2,3)
> add.edge(n, 1,2)
> m <- as.matrix(n, "adjacency")
> sum(m) # here you are expecting 3
[1] 2
> as.matrix(n, "adjacency")
  1 2 3
1 0 1 0
2 0 0 1
3 0 0 0



~michal

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Three-Way Multidimentional Scaling
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Philip.  I don't know of any easy way to do it, but one possibility is to concatenate the 8 matrices into a single 80x11 matrix, then read this in using read.table, convert it to a matrix using as.matrix, and finally convert it to a 10x8x11 array using
a <- array(my_80x11_matrix, dim=c(10,8,11))

You can then access, say, the 3rd 10x11 sub-matrix using a[,3,].  As for computing the distance matrix, I think you'd want to use the apply function for this purpose.

Best,
Dave

mod <- ergm(network ~ edges + gwesp(0, fixed=T) + nodefactor("code") +

messages.subject: [statnet_help] follow-up question on "structural zeroes"
messages.body_plain:
greetings,

a while ago i had a question about modeling directed two-mode data, and have something of a follow-up about this question. thanks to the guidance steve provided, it seemed that while statnet is not able to model bipartite directed networks, i could basically treat my network as unipartite but include terms in my models for "homophily" within each mode... ergm would then recognize that no within-mode ties existed, fix these parameters at negative infinity, and respect this restriction during parameter estimation.

i have another situation where certain actors are not allowed to contact each other- but these "impossible" ties are not structured in such a way that i can model them with nodematch terms. in other words, they are something like "structural zeroes" in the language of RSiena- and i would like to estimate a model that respects this restriction where some ties are not possible. my first thought was to follow the same approach as above, but instead of using nodematch terms to identify the "impossible" ties, i would do the same thing with an edgecov term. when i run this model, however, ergm does not seem to recognize that these ties are impossible in the same way it does for the nodematch situation... and so instead of getting a parameter that is fixed at negative infinity, i simply get a parameter estimate that is strongly negative (say, -16) and becomes even more strongly negative with each MCMC iteration.

my question, then, is whether this approach is problematic for any reason? or is this actually a reasonable way to impose "structural zeroes" in the model? it seems the ideal case would be to be able to fix this parameter at negative infinity... but if there is not currently a way to do this, i want to make sure the approach i've taken in practice (i.e. letting the edgecov parameter work its way to an unstable, but strongly negative value) is not creating other issues of which i'm unaware. any help would be greatly appreciated! thanks,

-kevin

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] RE: Generating graphs with a fixed minimum distance
messages.body_plain:
Making your graphs bigger and your tie probability smaller works.

> results<-matrix(NA,nrow=10,ncol=100)
> for(x in 1:10){
+   for(y in 1:dim(results)[2]){
+     g<-rgraph(1000,tprob=1/(2^x))
+     d<-geodist(g)$gdist
+     results[x,y]<-max(d[is.finite(d)])}}
> plot(cbind((2^(1:10),rowMeans(results)))

(this takes a while to run)

This shows that for a 1000 node random network, a probability of a tie of about 1/200 should yield a max distance of 10.
Verified below:

> maxGeo <- function(x){
+ g<-rgraph(1000,tprob=1/200)
+ d<-geodist(g)$gdist
+ return(max(d[is.finite(d)]))}
> mean(unlist(lapply(list(1:100),FUN=maxGeo)))
[1] 10

Hope this helps!
Cheers
Brian

I have a question that seems pretty simple, but I haven't been able to find out a clear answer about it yet.


I have directed network data with a valued trait (X), and my theory stipulates the following:

1.? actors high in X will send fewer ties to others (actor-level hypothesis -- nodeocov)

?

Also, I'm using "edgecov" to denote raw difference in X between nodes (using a matrix of difference scores), rather than the absolute difference term (absdiff), because point #3 above indicates raw difference as the important issue. Is it appropriate to include this edgecov term alongside the other two terms (nodeocov and nodeicov), or is there too much redundant information in the model?



thanks,
markus schafer
dept of sociology

messages.subject: [statnet_help] RE: Differential Reciprocity
messages.body_plain:
dear justin,

please forgive me if i am misunderstanding- but don't the current versions of the mutual terms allow you to study the effect you are interested in? in other words, if you include the generic "mutual" term in your model capturing the baseline tendency for EVERYONE towards reciprocity; and then you include another term in your model capturing reciprocity only among people who match on the "leader" attribute (or, if you want you can set diff=TRUE and have separate terms for reciprocity between two leaders, on one hand, and reciprocity between two non-leaders, on the other)- then this latter term will provide the same effect you are interested in, except its opposite. in other words, for instance, if you find that the reciprocity*matching term is negative- indicating that (controlling for the baseline tendency towards reciprocity) reciprocal ties between two people who match on leadership are LESS likely than chance would predict- then by definition reciprocal ties between two people who do not match on leadership (i.e. a leader and a non-leader) are MORE likely than chance would predict. so- all things equal- if you want to find the likelihood of a "matching" reciprocal tie, you add the baseline reciprocity coefficient to the matching*reciprocity coefficient (plus any other matching/sociality terms as appropriate); whereas if you want the likelihood of a "non-matching" reciprocal tie, you just look to the baseline reciprocity coefficient (plus any other matching/sociality terms as appropriate).

please let me know if this doesn't make sense (or if anyone else has any corrections!). best wishes,

-kevin

Kevin Lewis
Assistant Professor of Sociology
University of California, San Diego

From: statnet_help-bounces@mailman2.u.washington.edu [mailto:statnet_help-bounces@mailman2.u.washington.edu] On Behalf Of Kirkland, Justin H
Sent: Wednesday, December 05, 2012 10:56 AM
To: statnet_help@u.washington.edu
Subject: [statnet_help] Differential Reciprocity

Dear Statnet Users and Developers,

I am working on a project attempting to measure the reciprocity between sets of legislators in the Texas state legislature. In general, I expect reciprocity to be common, but I expect that reciprocity will be even more common when one of the members of a dyad is a leader in the legislature. That is, I expect that {i,j} and {j,i} will occur together frequently, but I expect that frequency to be even higher when j has a certain node attribute. I have been trying to figure out ways to implement an ERGM to test this expectation in R, but have had little success. The standard "mutual" term for for ERGMs will allow node attributes to be incorporated, but this will result in a statistic measuring reciprocity when both i and j are leaders or when both are not leaders. I cannot figure out how to generate a "mutual" term for the circumstance where j is a leader and i is not.

My instinct is that I may have to build a new ERGM term using the ergm.userterms package. This package requires new functions both in R and in C (since ergm change statistics are calculated using C). Unfortunately, I have little experience programming in C, so designing such a statistic is beyond my current skills. I believe I could make some head way if I could locate the original C code of the basic "mutual" term for ERGMs, but have had little success tracking down the C code for "mutual" either on my own machine or through internet searches.

If anyone has any insights about:

1) How I might test the differential reciprocity I expect using the current terms in the ERGM toolkit,
2) How to code up such a statistic using the ergm.userterms package, or
3) What the C code for the standard "mutual" ergm term looks like

it would be of a great help to me. I am currently using R 2.15 and stat net version 3.0-1 on a Macintosh. Thanks in advance for any help!

Best,
Justin Kirkland

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Combining UCINET Adj.Matrices with categorical data in excel
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Combining UCINET Adj.Matrices with categorical data in excel
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statneters,

I am a relative newcomer to R and am looking to merge my work in networks
with the conventional scale data I have on an organisation (p=58).
I have a large number of processed binary adjacency matrices developed in
UCINET, which I can output as excel files. I also have a large number of
data frames within excel files.
The AM's and the excel files all share a common coding so 1 identifies the
same person in the network as it does in the attribute dataframes.

I would like to explore how much of the network analysis I can do in
Statnet/R. At present I am finding it hard to know how I might most
conveniently link the AM's to the various categorical data I have (e.g.
personality, values, perceived trustworthiness and so on).
I would like to be able to carry out both ego and network correlations and
regressions.
For example I might want to regress personality profile on network
centrality (there is not uniformity of number of edges between the network
data and the attribute data, some attribute data may apply to a subset of
the network e.g. managers).

I have looked through a number of the supporting documents, and found
'Network Analysis with statnet for Individual , Organizational , and
International Relations Applications' to be particularly helpful.
But, it looks as though I would need to code each attribute link
individually which would not be practical.
My guess (fervent hope...) is that there is a simple way of knitting these
data together that I have not registered.

Please don't hesitate to ask if more information/clarification is needed.

Any help or link to a suitable document on this would make my jubilee
weekend!

Best,
Nick Duncan
University of Cambridge

messages.body_plain:
Shai --

Thanks so much for the nice comments :-)  Always good to hear that people 
appreciate these tools.

We offer workshops every year at the Sunbelt conference (if you're not 
familiar with INSNA, this is their annual conference for social network 
analysts).  This past year, we offered 6 separate workshops that covered 
everything from the basics to the new dynamic functionality and writing 
custom ergm terms.  We'll be doing so in 2013 again, and the conference 
will be in Hamburg: http://www.insna.org/sunbelt.html

Carter Butts and his team also give workshops at the annual Political 
Methodology conference.

And Steve Goodreau and I will be starting a workshop on using statnet for 
epidemic modeling this year at the UW that will be taught every summer.

best,
Martina

messages.body_plain:
Hello!

Our data is about sociolinguistic relations of several teenage students 
(12 years old) in sociocentric networks of multiple schools. The 
sociolinguistic relations have two types of information: relations 
between adolescents and language used in this relation. Not all dyads 
have relations, and if relations exist, can be in language A or language 
B. Our information can be more complex, because language use is in 
language A, language B, language A and B, o other languages. But we can 
dichotomize the data.

We have problems with the analysis of our data, because edges have 
attributes, and and I couldn't find any reference about how to handle 
whit it, neither with R nor any other software.

Then, I have three questions:

How can we analyse edge attributes with ERGM? Is it possible? A possible 
way is work with multiple networks, like "relations in language A" and 
"relations in language B". As I see in (few) previous posts in this 
direction in this mail list, high statistical knowledge is needed to 
proceed. Out of R, it is possible compare networks with ERG Models with 
XPnet. But our data is (theorically) negative correspondence, and can't 
interpret results of multiple networks analysis like it. Do you know 
bibliography that can help us?

How can we analyse valued networks (qualitative links) with "sna"? We 
are interested in multiple analysis at the descriptive level:: language 
reciprocity, centrality in different languages, triad analysis with 
multiple languages relations, and so on...  We are working it combining 
UCINET results of full network, and network in language A and network in 
language B, and comparing it with Excel. Is it possible analyse wit 
"sna" how reciprocity dyads have language reciprocity too? For exemple, 
"90% of reciprocity relations are in the same language". Or 20% of 
transitive triads use A language in X -> Y and Y -> Z relations, and B 
language in X -> Z relation. We are also interested in some analysis 
with "sna" like UCINET> Tools> Testing Hypotheses> Mixed Dyadic / Nodal> 
Categorical attributes> Relational Contingency Table analysis.

Maybe a solution is working with signed networks. Origins of this 
analysis is other, about positive relations (friends) and negative 
relations (enemies). And balanced networks theory don't adjust to 
language networks. But is not far that language use in networks can be 
understanded  like relations in A language (+), in B language (-) or in 
both languages (0). How can we work with signed networks in "statnet"?

Last but not least, my presentation in Statnet mailing list: I am Natxo 
Sorolla, and I am working in sociology of language at the University of 
Barcelona.

Natxo Sorolla

messages.subject: [statnet_help] including nodeicov, nodeocov, and edgecov in same model
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] including nodeicov, nodeocov, and edgecov in same model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Markus,

What you propose as a model is possible, depending on the parameterization 
you use.  The design is a bit like a mixing matrix with dyads cross 
tabulated by attribute X.  Your model has row and column effects, and an 
"upper triangle" effect.

What you need to be clear about is whether the magnitude of (X_i - X_j) 
matters.  If not, you can construct a binary indicator for the edgecov, 
and the terms will not be collinear.  If the magnitude matters, but only 
when the difference is < 0, the edgecov will =0 for cases when the diff is 
>0, so will still not be collinear.  You may still run into some 
difficulties estimating this, depending on the size of your 
sample and distribution of your data.

What you can't do is put the difference in, along with the values of X_i 
and X_j, but it sounds like your theory would not lead to that 
operationalization anyway.

hth,
Martina

messages.subject: [statnet_help] question about simulation
messages.body_plain:
Ya,

The purpose is to be able to simulate a *dynamic* network (edges 
forming and dissolving, and perhaps nodes entering and leaving), that 
preserves the properties observed in the single cross-sectional snapshot 
from your data.  Your data are just a single draw from the real underlying 
dynamic network.

Martina

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Differential Reciprocity
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet Users and Developers,

I am working on a project attempting to measure the reciprocity between sets of legislators in the Texas state legislature. In general, I expect reciprocity to be common, but I expect that reciprocity will be even more common when one of the members of a dyad is a leader in the legislature. That is, I expect that {i,j} and {j,i} will occur together frequently, but I expect that frequency to be even higher when j has a certain node attribute. I have been trying to figure out ways to implement an ERGM to test this expectation in R, but have had little success. The standard "mutual" term for for ERGMs will allow node attributes to be incorporated, but this will result in a statistic measuring reciprocity when both i and j are leaders or when both are not leaders. I cannot figure out how to generate a "mutual" term for the circumstance where j is a leader and i is not.

My instinct is that I may have to build a new ERGM term using the ergm.userterms package. This package requires new functions both in R and in C (since ergm change statistics are calculated using C). Unfortunately, I have little experience programming in C, so designing such a statistic is beyond my current skills. I believe I could make some head way if I could locate the original C code of the basic "mutual" term for ERGMs, but have had little success tracking down the C code for "mutual" either on my own machine or through internet searches.

If anyone has any insights about:

1) How I might test the differential reciprocity I expect using the current terms in the ERGM toolkit,
2) How to code up such a statistic using the ergm.userterms package, or
3) What the C code for the standard "mutual" ergm term looks like

it would be of a great help to me. I am currently using R 2.15 and stat net version 3.0-1 on a Macintosh. Thanks in advance for any help!

Best,
Justin Kirkland

Hi Peter,

I'm not sure if this answer your question. If the structural zeroes you mention refer to the impossibility of nodes of group A being connected with nodes of group B (since it's bipartite); then the package you need is networksis, which is part of statnet. Check the paper: 

1.	Admiraal, R. & Handcock, M. S. Networksis: a package to simulate bipartite graphs with fixed marginals through sequential importance sampling. Journal of statistical software 24, 1?21 (2008).

By fixing the matrix marginals (sum of rows and cols) in the modeling process they deal with the structural zeroes. I hope that helps. Otherwise, sorry for the noise.

Best,

Juan
